A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same iterative value-guided decoding work despite the title and method renaming. The complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original summarization, dialogue, instruction-following, jailbreak-safety, ablation, transferability, and inference-time results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including reward comparisons, GPT-4 win rates, safety rates, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: IVO becomes IVR, with Monte Carlo Value Estimation and Iterative On-Policy Optimization renamed Value Exploration and Iterative Self-Refinement. Algorithm 1, reward targets, losses, iterative updates, and decoding procedures remain equivalent; sampling from the current policy was already implemented in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use TL;DR, Anthropic HH, UltraFeedback/Alpaca-Eval 2, and the attack-enhanced SALAD-Bench scenario. Model-size transfer and aligned/unaligned safety coverage are also retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain ARGS, FUDGE, and VAS for summarization/dialogue, online DPO and IPO for dialogue, and FUDGE and VAS for instruction following. Table 1 adds a compute column for its existing comparator set.

E3.justification: v3 adds estimated training FLOPs as an efficiency metric in Table 1, explicitly scoped to a single training batch. Existing sample sizes, splits, model configurations, training schedules, decoding settings, and quality-evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The trajectory-count and iteration ablations, model-size transfer analysis, jailbreak tests, and tokenwise-versus-blockwise sampling analysis are retained. The four appendix case studies contain identical prompts and responses after accounting for the method rename.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds and retain the uncertainty bands and error bars in Figures 2–5. No new uncertainty definitions, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are supplied.

E6.justification: Table 1 newly reports estimated FLOPs: 0.25 × 10^15 for FUDGE and VAS, 4.00 × 10^15 for DPO and IPO, and 2.00 × 10^15 for IVR. Existing win rates, reward curves, safety results, ablations, transfer scores, and inference-time ratios are unchanged.

T1.justification: The MDP definitions, policy equations, and training objectives remain equivalent. v1 Section 4.3's visitation measure, partial-coverage assumption, and optimality-gap argument move to v3 Appendix B without a substantive mathematical revision or new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution drop the explicit variance-reduction claim and foreground bridging the distributional gap through broader trajectory coverage and iterative refinement. The principal alignment, computational-efficiency, task-generality, and 77.52% dialogue win-rate claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new FLOP estimates as requiring half the training computation of DPO/IPO under its settings. Its limitations omit v1's explicit warning that repeated collection and value-function updates increase training time; base-policy dependence and the safety-related interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Table 1 adds estimated training-resource information and specifies its single-batch scope, although no estimation recipe or hardware details accompany it. The implementation recipes, hyperparameters, decoding settings, judge prompt, and access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work is condensed, removing discussion and citations concerning in-context alignment, representation editing, and PPO variants, including Lin et al. (2023) and Kong et al. (2024). The central positioning relative to value-guided decoding and online RLHF is retained.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, and method narrative around the renamed framework. It combines the component descriptions, moves related work and the coverage argument to appendices, moves limitations into the main text and the impact statement into an appendix, and removes duplicated safety discussion.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different page and appendix layout. Figure 1 is redesigned from a three-dimensional reward illustration into a two-panel distribution-gap/framework diagram; existing plots are resized and relocated, Table 1 gains a FLOP column, and the unchanged judge template becomes Figure 6.

improvement.justification: The revised narrative and Figure 1 explain the iterative mechanism more clearly, while Table 1 makes the training-efficiency comparison more concrete through explicitly scoped estimates. These provide a modest overall gain. Shortened related-work coverage and removal of the iterative-training-cost caveat reduce context, and the estimates do not establish total pipeline savings; the underlying empirical and theoretical validation remains unchanged.
